capture.auto_open.fails: This browser does not let Ferret open the popup by itself, so only the badge shows.
capture.auto_open.hint: The popup opens by itself only on the page you are looking at, and a click on it is ignored for a moment so a click meant for the page cannot answer the offer.
capture.auto_open.off: Off. Ferret only puts a badge on its button when there is an offer.
capture.auto_open.on: On. After you submit a form, Ferret opens its popup with the offer, if the browser allows it. The badge on the button always shows that an offer waits.
capture.auto_open.switch: Open Ferret by itself when there is an offer
capture.error.disconnected: Ferret's background stopped while it worked. Open this page again.
capture.error.not_available: Saving passwords is not part of this version of Ferret.
capture.error.permission_missing: The browser did not give Ferret access to https pages, so nothing was turned on.
capture.error.permission_refused: You did not allow access to https pages, so nothing was turned on.
capture.error.register_failed: The browser would not start the script. Nothing was turned on.
capture.error.unknown: That did not work. Nothing was changed.
capture.never.empty: No sites yet. Choosing "Never for this site" on an offer adds one here.
capture.never.hint: Ferret offers nothing for these sites. A site you chose in a private window stays here only until the browser closes.
capture.never.remove.label: Remove {host} from the list
capture.never.title: Sites you never want to be asked about
capture.off: Off. Ferret does not look at the forms you submit.
capture.off_access_given: Off. Ferret does not look at the forms you submit. It already has access to https pages, so turning it on does not ask again.
capture.on: On. Ferret offers to save a new password or update a changed one after you submit a form.
capture.reload: Tabs that are already open start to notice passwords after you reload them.
capture.switch: Offer to save and update passwords
capture.title: Offer to save passwords
capture.why: To notice a new or changed password, Ferret has to run a small script on every https page, and so it asks the browser for access to https pages. The script changes nothing on a page and sends nothing until you submit a form with a password in it. What you typed is kept only in the memory of Ferret's background page, for at most five minutes, and is dropped when the vault locks. Nothing is saved without your click on the offer. Ferret never asks for your master password inside a web page.
